bullets.title: Jensen Huang teases undisclosed Nvidia surprise product; robotics and PC ARM chips in focus
bullets.body: Fintwit analysts note Jensen's track record of only teasing products that exist and ship, making the undisclosed 'surprise' announcement significant. Top candidates cited: Nvidia's ARM laptop chips (N1, N1X) competing directly with Intel/AMD for the PC market—with Intel CEO hinting at a joint product—and a dedicated robotics/physical AI brain chip. Quantum computing linkage (Nvidia software connecting quantum machines to GPUs) also flagged as potential.

bullets.title: Snowflake monster quarter signals AI software monetization is real; 'AI Ghost' narrative collapsing
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flagged Snowflake's strong quarter as evidence that AI is now monetizing at the software layer, noting a sequential pattern: 'First Palantir, then Datadog, now Snowflake all showing positive AI business results.' Salesforce Agentforce cited as additional confirmation that enterprise AI adoption is accelerating, disproving the skeptical 'AI Ghost' thesis.

bullets.title: Semiconductors trading above 200-DMA by widest margin since dot-com crash; rally has overshot EPS
bullets.body: @themarketear (RT'd by a major fintwit account) warns the recent semiconductor rally has 'overshot near-term EPS revisions' and is 'disconnected from fundamental EPS support.' Separately, semis are trading above their 200-day moving average by the largest margin since the dot-com bubble burst—flagged as a potential valuation red flag.

bullets.title: AI token pricing 'race to the bottom' compared to Groupon subsidy wars by Goldman Delta One head
bullets.body: Goldman's Delta One head Rich Privorotsky warned that token economics are resembling Groupon-era subsidy dynamics: DeepSeek cut token pricing by 75% and Xiaomi's MiMo slashed pricing by ~99%, risking a destructive race to the bottom for AI infrastructure margins.

bullets.title: Macro bear case: equity EPS assumptions require historically implausible 10% nominal GDP growth
bullets.body: A credible fintwit macro analyst argues current equity valuations are extrapolating the strongest 5-year earnings growth in history, requiring ~10% annual nominal GDP growth—roughly 2x the pace of the last decade and only seen at peak 1970s inflation—plus unsustainable consumer dissavings on top of that.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mostly lower in premarket: NVDA -1.1%, TSLA -1.3%, MSFT +0.9%
bullets.body: Premarket movers showed the Magnificent 7 broadly under pressure: Tesla -1.3%, Nvidia -1.1%, Alphabet -0.5%, Amazon -0.4%, Apple -0.2%, with Meta +0.2% and Microsoft +0.9% as relative outperformers. S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures extended losses intraday.

bullets.title: SPY/QQQ showing bearish divergences on daily chart; 9 consecutive green weeks for S&P 500
bullets.body: One fintwit account issued a 'warning' that SPY and QQQ are forming bearish divergences on the daily timeframe, with markets showing exhaustion and choppy price action expected even if marginal new highs occur. Separately, the S&P 500 has now posted 20 all-time highs in 2026 and is on track for its 9th consecutive green week—longest streak since 2023.

bullets.title: PCE inflation expected at 3.8% headline; Fed's credibility on 2% target questioned
bullets.body: Consensus expects headline PCE to print at 3.8% annualized (core steady at 3.3%) on a heavy economic data day. A prominent macro commentator asks when the Fed will 'come clean' on a de facto shift from a 2% to 3% inflation target, given the persistent overshoot.

bullets.title: ECB accounts: inflation risks intensifying, some members may have preferred higher rates
bullets.body: ECB meeting accounts released this morning showed general agreement that no strong second-round effects have emerged yet, but upside inflation risks and downside growth risks have both intensified. Some members may have supported higher rates than implemented, and the close vote suggests ongoing policy tension.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk: Iran fires missile toward Kuwait, stops vessels in Hormuz Strait
bullets.body: Multiple breaking headlines flagged Iran firing a missile toward Kuwait (intercepted), stopping two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, and asserting mandatory coordination requirements for Hormuz transit. The EU's Oil Coordination Group warned of a tighter jet fuel market 'within weeks' if Hormuz situation doesn't improve, and S&P/Nasdaq futures extended losses on the news.

bullets.title: InP laser capacity expected to grow 12-20x from 2025-2030 for AI optical interconnects
bullets.body: A fintwit account focused on photonics flagged a notable data point: InP laser capacity is expected to increase approximately 12-20x from 2025 to 2030, with vendors taking a 'conservative stance' aligned toward the ~12x figure. Relevant to the AI optical interconnect supply chain.

bullets.title: Ayar Labs-Wiwynn CPO partnership flagged as potentially material for cloud rack-scale deployments
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst called the Ayar Labs announcement with Wiwynn 'potentially very material' for CPO-to-rack-scale deployments, noting Wiwynn's cloud clients include Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft, with Google TPU discussions also underway. Relevant for tracking hyperscaler optical interconnect sourcing trends.

bullets.title: Consumer stress signals accumulating: student loan delinquencies at 4-year high, mortgage apps -8.5%
bullets.body: NY Fed data shows 10.3% of student loan balances are 90+ days delinquent—highest since 2020. MBA mortgage applications fell 8.5% week-over-week with refinancings down 18.1% as mortgage rates hit 9-month highs. Average new car payments reached $767/month in 4Q25, with rolled-over underwater loans hitting $916/month.

bullets.title: CEO confidence retreats back into negative territory in 2Q26
bullets.body: The Conference Board CEO Confidence Index declined from 59 in 1Q26 to 47 in 2Q26, falling back below the neutral 50 threshold after a brief quarter of optimism. The deterioration aligns with persistent inflation and trade uncertainty narratives dominating macro commentary.

bullets.title: USD 1-year forward rates shift meaningfully higher; JPMorgan warns long-term dollar weakness ahead
bullets.body: Market structure commentary flagged that USD 1-year forward rates have shifted meaningfully higher across the entire term structure relative to both 1-month and 3-month ago. Contrasting this near-term dollar strength, JPMorgan's EMEA CEO warned that US fiscal dynamics will drive long-term USD structural depreciation.

bullets.title: CVS adds Lilly's Zepbound to preferred drug list in reversal
bullets.body: CVS reversed a prior decision and added Eli Lilly's Zepbound (tirzepatide) to its preferred drug list—a positive development for GLP-1 market access and Lilly's commercial positioning.

bullets.title: MSFT seen as relative safe haven in market downturn; already retraced more than peers
bullets.body: One fintwit account positioned Microsoft as a 'safer' holding during broad market weakness, arguing MSFT has already undergone a more significant retracement than peers and would go down 'less' in a risk-off environment.

bullets.title: Richmond Fed Manufacturing hits 55.4 in May; ADP private payrolls slow
bullets.body: Richmond Fed Manufacturing Index expanded for a third consecutive month, hitting 55.4 in May on an ISM-adjusted basis. ADP private payrolls slowed to 35,750 jobs/week average for the four weeks ending May 9, down from 40,750 in the prior period—a softening labor market signal.

bullets.title: S&P 500 top 10 companies now ~40% of index; concentration risk flagged
bullets.body: A fintwit account noted the ten largest S&P 500 companies now comprise nearly 40% of total index market cap, flagging elevated concentration risk as markets hit new all-time highs. The observation echoes growing concerns about passive flows amplifying mega-cap dominance.
